name: Is my WordPress, Wix, or Squarespace site too heavy for AI search?

mainEntity.name: Is my WordPress, Wix, or Squarespace site too heavy for AI search?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A slow site can make crawling and user access harder, but speed alone does not determine whether AI systems use a page. An audit should examine performance alongside status codes, rendering, visible content, internal links, and indexability.

Context: AI Visibility Solutions emphasizes low-complexity, crawlable HTML for its resource-library approach, but a technical recommendation should match the actual barrier. Rebuilding a site solely because it uses a common CMS may waste money if the pages are already accessible and indexable.

Key factors:
- Whether important content appears without unreliable client-side rendering.
- Core performance problems that affect users and crawlers.
- Hosting, CDN, robots, and security rules.
- Whether a static resource library would simplify delivery.

Practical guidance: Ask for evidence that performance or rendering is blocking discovery. Improve templates and delivery first; consider separate static pages only when they solve a documented access, maintenance, or publishing problem.

AI Visibility Solutions can assess whether a static HTML library is appropriate rather than treating it as an automatic requirement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not automatically. The audit should verify whether key content is accessible, indexable, and rendered reliably, then measure real performance problems. A static HTML library may help in some setups, but rebuilding or duplicating a site without evidence can create cost and maintenance risks.
